title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant - Part-Time

Location: Headlands Grove, Swindon

Hours: Tuesday and Wednesday, 8:00am-4:00pm

Break: 30-minute unpaid break each day

Total: 15 hours per week

Salary: £30,000 per annum (pro rata £12,000 pa)

Pay: Weekly

Contract: Permanent, part-time

A part-time role with plenty to get involved in

We're looking for an organised, dependable and detail-focused Accounts Assistant to join the team.

Working closely with our Head of Accounts, you'll help keep the day-to-day finances running smoothly-from processing invoices and reconciling statements to answering queries and supporting the wider Accounts Department.

This isn't a role where you'll simply be left to enter figures all day. We're looking for someone who enjoys taking ownership of their work, spotting when something doesn't look quite right and helping to keep an important part of the business organised and on track.

What you'll be doing
- Processing supplier invoices and credit notes accurately
- Matching invoices against purchase orders and supporting documents
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date purchase ledger records
- Reconciling supplier statements and investigating discrepancies
- Responding to supplier and internal payment queries
- Supporting payment preparation and account reconciliations
- Processing expenses and other financial documentation
- Keeping accounting records organised and easy to access
- Assisting the Head of Accounts with day-to-day financial administration
- Getting involved with wider finance duties and reporting when needed

What we're looking for

You'll ideally have previous experience in an accounts, finance or purchase ledger role, but just as importantly, you'll be someone who is:
- Confident working with numbers and financial information
- Naturally organised with excellent attention to detail
- Comfortable using accounting software and Microsoft Excel
- Able to manage priorities and meet deadlines
- Happy to work independently while remaining part of the wider team
- Professional, approachable and confident communicating with suppliers and colleagues
- Willing to ask questions, solve problems and take responsibility for getting things right

Why join?

You'll be joining an established and growing home-improvement business in a role that offers fixed weekday hours, a supportive working environment and the opportunity to make a genuine contribution to the Accounts Department.

If you enjoy bringing order to the numbers, solving the occasional financial mystery and being the person others can rely on, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Administrator
description:
We are looking for a detail-focused, team-oriented Administrator (internally known as a Service Delivery Assistant) to join our team in Wiltshire. This role is to provide vital administrative support, helping to ensure the effective delivery of services and maintain high standards of service provision for victims of crime.

This is a part-time position, worked across 15 hours per week, and we would be happy to discuss preferred working days and hours at interview. The role is home-based, with frequent travel across Wiltshire to support service delivery, attend meetings, and participate in training and other work-related activities.

Do you want to make a difference every day? Do you want to contribute to change & improvement for those who need it?

Do you have resilience & adaptability? Can you work effectively with a focus on customer service and care?

If yes, then we'd love to hear from you

What we offer

At Victim Support, we are committed to attracting and retaining the best talent. Our competitive rewards and benefits package includes:
- Flexible Working Options: Including hybrid working.
- Generous Annual Leave: 28 days plus Bank Holidays, increasing to 33 days plus Bank Holidays, with options to buy or sell annual leave.
- Birthday Leave: An extra day off for your birthday.
- Pension Plan: 5% employer contribution.
- Enhanced Allowances: Enhanced sick pay, maternity, and paternity payments.
- Exclusive Discounts: High Street, retail, holiday, gym, entertainment, and leisure discounts.
- Financial Wellbeing: Access to our financial wellbeing hub and salary-deducted finance.
- Wellbeing Support: Employee assistance programme and wellbeing support.
- Inclusive Networks: Access to EDI networks and colleague cafes.
- Sustainable Travel: Cycle to work scheme and season ticket loans.
- Career Development: Ongoing training and support with opportunities for career progression.

About the Role

As a Service Delivery Assistant, you will you will provide high-quality administrative support to the team and service. You will act as a first point of contact for enquiries into the service and support the wider team with administrative duties.

Key Responsibilities:
- Upload referrals to our computerised case management system, in accordance with our standards
- Manage incoming and outgoing mail, telephone and general queries for the service
- Collate and supply information and correspondence to internal and external contacts
- Liaise with referring agencies to improve referral information and support referral pathways
- Provide general admin support including data entry, minute taking, ordering office supplies, raising purchase orders and processing invoices.
- Help to coordinate external communication, management of local social media accounts and preparation of materials to help promote the service.

About You:

Ideally, you will have experience working within a client focused service and a good understanding and knowledge of office systems.

You will need:
- Effective verbal and written communication and numerical skills.
- Experience working in an administrative setting
- Experience of providing administrative support to a team
- Understanding and knowledge of the requirements relating to confidentiality and data protection.
- Understanding and knowledge of equal opportunities and diversity.
- Ability to prioritise own workload and deal with competing demands in an organised and methodical manner.
- Good IT skills and experience of using all packages in the standard Microsoft Office suite and case management systems/databases.
- Strong customer service skills with the ability to communicate sensitively and effectively both verbally and in writing with a wide range of individuals and audiences.
- Ability to work on own initiative and with minimal supervision to achieve deadlines.
- Strong record keeping skills with a focus on quality and accuracy.

About Us

Victim Support is an independent charity dedicated to supporting people affected by crime and traumatic incidents in England and Wales. We put them at the heart of our organisation and our support and campaigns are informed and shaped by them and their experiences.

Victim Support are committed to recruiting with care and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Background checks and Disclosed Barring Service checks may be required.

At Victim Support, we're proud to celebrate diversity and create a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We're committed to being an antiracist organisation, and we actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those from Black and Asian and other minoritised communities.

As a Disability Confident Employer, we will offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet all essential criteria for a job where it is practicable to do so. We are also happy to make reasonable adjustments during the recruitment and selection process.

How to apply

To apply for this role please follow the link below to the Jobs page on our website and complete the application form demonstrating how you meet the essential shortlisting criteria.

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, if we receive enough suitable applications to take forward to interview prior to the published closing date. If you have already registered & started an application, then we will contact you to advise of the amended closing date wherever possible.

title: Care Navigator/Administrator
description: North Swindon Practice is a busy, friendly and forward thinking GP Practice operating across two sites: Home Ground Surgery and Crossroads. We are committed to providing high quality, patient-centered care to our local community. We are looking to recruit a full time Care Navigator/Administrator to join our dedicated team. 37 hours per week, Mon-Fri with a finish time of 18:30 and this is non-negotiable. This is a key front of house and administrative role supporting patients, clinicians, and the wider practice team. Previous applicants need not apply. This is a fast-paced and sometimes highly stressful environment, where strong communication skills and the ability to remain calm under pressure are essential. You will be the first point of contact for our patients and play a vital part in ensuring the practice runs smoothly day-to-day. Key Responsibilities Welcoming patients and managing queries in person, by telephone and online Booking and managing appointments using clinical systems Supporting administrative processes such as scanning, coding, and correspondence Signposting patients appropriately in line with practice protocols Providing support to clinicians and the wider administrative team Ensuring patient confidentiality and data protection at all times Care Navigation & Patient Support Provide a warm, professional first point of contact for all patients. Use active signposting to direct patients to the most appropriate clinician, service or resource in line with practice protocols. Manage incoming telephone calls and online requests, ensuring urgent issues are identified and escalated promptly. Assist patients in understanding digital access routes ie online systems and NHS App. Communicate clearly, sensitively and respectfully when supporting vulnerable or distressed patients. Reception Duties Welcome patients and manage face to face enquiries at the reception desk. Book, amend and manage appointments using clinical systems. Process prescription requests, sick notes, referrals and other administrative tasks following practice guidelines. Handle payments and issue receipts where applicable. Maintain a calm, organised front desk environment, even during busy periods. Administrative Support Process and route incoming clinical correspondence, pathology results, and documentation. Perform accurate scanning, coding and workflow management using digital systems. Maintain patient records in line with practice and NHS data standards. Support administrative projects such as audits, data quality improvement and service development. Confidentiality & Compliance Adhere to strict confidentiality and data protection policies at all times. Respect patient privacy and maintain secure handling of all personal data. Follow practice policies, health and safety procedures, safeguarding standards and infection control protocols. Communication & Teamwork Work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team, supporting colleagues and sharing information effectively. Attend staff meetings, mandatory training and development sessions. Demonstrate a positive, flexible attitude and willingness to support the wider team during periods of high demand.

title: GP Receptionist
description: The purpose of the Receptionist role is to provide a high-quality, professional reception and administrative service to patients, doctors, staff, colleagues, and other healthcare professionals, portraying the Practice in the highest possible professional manner. Receptionists are responsible for ensuring patients can access the healthcare services they need efficiently and courteously. They play a key role in supporting the day-to-day running of the practice and in ensuring the smooth flow of communication between patients and staff. Flexibility is essential for this role, and you will be required to provide additional cover during staff holidays or sickness. - Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the practice. - Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. - Use your own judgment and communication skills. - Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover, and ensure procedures are completed. - Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. - Enter requests for home visits into the clinical system, ensuring to carefully record all relevant details and referring to the rota doctor where necessary. - Enter patient information on to the computer as required. - Open and distribute incoming mail. - Photocopy and shred documentation. - Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. - When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. - Keep the reception area, noticeboards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter. - Assist with the induction of new reception staff. - Support reception team members in managing busy periods and resolving patient queries effectively. - Process new patient registrations and action patient deductions. - Any other delegated duties considered appropriate to the post.

title: GP Senior Receptionist
description: Priory Road Medical Centre are looking to recruit someone who is capable of working in a busy environment and confident at dealing with a wide ranging patient group. It will involve face-to-face and telephone work. You should be a team player who is able to help meet the targets required by this busy team and are adaptable to the needs of the practice. The job is for 25 hours per week Mon to Fri 1.00pm to 6.00pm Telephone and front desk appointment bookings Prescription handling Scanning documentation General call handling/administrative duties JOB TITLE: SENIOR RECEPTIONIST SUPERVISOR: RESPONSIBLE FOR: The provision of an efficient and caring service to the patients of the Practice. DUTIES GENERAL RECEPTION To maintain strict confidentiality at all times. To open the premises if required, open shutters, check heating and ventilation and turn off the alarm. Ready the premises for work. To lock up the premises if required, closing shutters and switching on intruder alarm and generally securing the building. A doctor should always be present on your departure. To ensure that enquiries from patients are efficiently and courteously handled. To ensure that the filing, record keeping and distribution of documents is undertaken efficiently and promptly. To receive and route patients and visitors on their arrival. Answer general enquiries, explain surgery procedures, make new and routine appointments. File and extract records and any documents relating to these. Implement actions as defined by the doctors and nurses in relation to Test Results. Receive and record requests for home visits. Ensure that adequate supplies of stationery, towels and couch rolls area available in the consulting rooms and reception area. Take messages for all members of the Primary Care Team and record them accurately on the computer, ensuring that messages are passed on promptly. Tidy reception area and check cleanliness of patients toilet. Attend staff meetings and Away Days as requested. Accept requests from patients for completion of forms, eg. medicals etc. by GPs and informing patients if a fee is payable. Taking and entering fees for non NHS work in the petty cash book, giving change and verifying cheques. Giving patients receipts for monies received. Using and processing card machine. Photocopy documents as and when required. Shred confidential documents as and when required. Issue computerised prescriptions. Clear up spills, eg. vomit, blood, when necessary according to Practice protocol. Maintain the items in the spills bucket. Attend training courses as and when requested, to do so for the mutual benefit of the employee and employer, on the understanding that no expense will be incurred by the individual save for refreshments. DUTIES SENIOR RECEPTIONIST Supervise, support and coordinate the Reception Team, ensuring effective day-to-day operations and high standards of patient service. Create agendas, chair and coordinate regular Reception Team and GP/Reception meetings, recording and communicating actions as required. Act as the main point of contact between the reception team, clinical staff, administration staff and management, ensuring information, protocols, procedures and updates are communicated effectively. Coordinate the promotion and organisation of practice campaigns, including annual Flu Clinics, ensuring adequate reception cover and efficient patient flow. Monitor and record reception staff sickness, annual leave and overtime, maintaining accurate records within the reception diary. Manage the reception email inbox and provide support to administrative staff in monitoring and managing safeguarding communications. Train, mentor and induct new reception staff, providing ongoing support and guidance to ensure competency and adherence to practice procedures. Conduct regular team supervision and provide support with staff development, performance management and day-to-day operational issues. Meet regularly with the Operations Manager to discuss service delivery, team performance, staffing matters, patient feedback and operational improvements. Ensure confidentiality is maintained at all times and that all practice policies and procedures are followed. Identify opportunities to improve reception processes and contribute to the continuous development of administrative systems and patient services. Carry out any other duties as reasonably requested and mutually agreed between employer and employee.
